question.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼\text{Exp}(\theta )$ and unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ The log-likelihood function of the sample $3.1,\,6.5,\,4.8,\,7.2$ is

$$
l(\theta )=a\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +b\theta .
$$

What is the value of $a+b?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i};\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent exponential random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x,\theta )=\theta {e}^{-\theta x},\,x\ge 0.
$$

Next, we write down the log-density function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡f(x,\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\theta {e}^{-\theta x}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta x}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta {x}_{i}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =n\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =3.1+6.5+4.8+7.2=21.6\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=4.$ Therefore,  

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta \cdot 21.6 \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(-21.6)\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=4+(-21.6)=-17.6.
$$
